intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square Evening Immersion
experiences.description: Skip the wasted late-arrival evening by heading straight to Djemaa el-Fna Square from your hotel — ideally staying in the Medina itself to walk there in minutes. As dusk falls, the square transforms into a living theatre of storytellers, musicians, snake charmers, and food stalls. Eat a full dinner here from the communal grills for under $5, making it the perfect low-cost, high-impact first-night experience that works even after a late flight arrival.

experiences.name: Medina Souks and Medersa Ben Youssef Guided Walk
experiences.description: Explore the labyrinthine souks of the Medina on foot with a local guide, visiting the 14th-century Medersa Ben Youssef — Morocco's largest historic Quranic school — and the nearby Marrakech Museum. Staying in a Medina riad puts you steps away, eliminating costly and time-consuming transfers. The guide helps you navigate dyers, spice merchants, and leather tanneries while providing deep historical context about the Almoravid and Saadian dynasties.
experiences.location: Northern Medina, near Ben Youssef Mosque, Marrakech

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Overnight Camel Trek and Berber Camp
experiences.description: Travel from Marrakech to Merzouga via a shared group transfer (book in advance to reduce cost). Trek by camel into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, spend the night in an authentic Berber nomad camp under a sky full of stars, enjoy traditional tagine dinner and live Gnawa drumming around the fire, then wake before dawn to watch the sunrise paint the dunes gold. This is the centrepiece adventure of the trip. To stay within budget, opt for a group shared camp package rather than a private luxury camp.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert, southeastern Morocco

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah Exploration
experiences.description: Stop at the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou en route to or from the Sahara — a natural itinerary addition that adds zero extra travel cost when using a shared group transfer. This ancient fortified village of earthen clay towers has appeared in Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Climb to the granary at the top for panoramic Atlas Mountain views and learn about the trans-Saharan trade routes that made this settlement vital for over a thousand years.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou, Ouarzazate Province, southern Morocco

experiences.name: Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs Cultural Half-Day
experiences.description: Dedicate a morning to two of Marrakech's most historically significant sites within walking distance of each other in the southern Medina. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with its intricate zellij tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. The nearby Saadian Tombs, sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917, house the ornate mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty. Both sites are within easy walking distance of Medina riads, keeping transport costs at zero and maximising your limited budget.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a budget-friendly petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-70 MAD) from the airport to your riad in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory walk through Jemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere — snake charmers, storytellers, and street musicians. Stroll into the northern edge of the souks to get a feel for the layout without pressure to buy. Visit the free exterior of the Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens for a peaceful rest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Grab a spot at one of the communal food stalls (stalls 1–100 area) for a lively, authentic Moroccan dinner experience. Walk back through the lit-up square and enjoy street performers before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a coffee and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) from a café near the riad for ~15 MAD
meals.lunch: Stop at a local snack stand near Jemaa el-Fna for harira soup and bread (~20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — merguez sausages, grilled kefta, and fresh orange juice (~60-80 MAD total)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for travel recovery. Negotiate all taxi fares before getting in. Keep your riad address written in Arabic to show drivers. Exchange some currency at the airport or an ATM (avoid hotel exchange rates).

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) — one of Marrakech's most stunning 19th-century palaces with intricate tilework and painted ceilings. Arrive before 9:30 AM to beat the crowds. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore its historic streets and the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the Souks of Marrakech — navigate through the dyers' souk (Souk Sabbaghin), leather souk, and spice souk. Practice bargaining and enjoy the sensory overload. Visit the free Ben Youssef Madrasa exterior area and explore the surrounding neighborhood. Stop at a local hammam for a traditional scrub experience (~80-120 MAD at a community hammam like Hammam Bab Doukkala).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the rooftop terrace of Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima for sunset views over the Medina (coffee ~25 MAD). Dinner in the Medina at a local restaurant away from the main square for more authentic and affordable food.

meals.breakfast: At your riad (if included) or a nearby café — mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (almond-argan dip) for ~30 MAD
meals.lunch: Local Medina restaurant — tagine with bread and a soft drink for ~60-80 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Brahim or similar local eatery — couscous or pastilla for ~70-90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven. The hammam experience is best in the afternoon before the evening rush. Carry small change for tips and entrance fees. Watch out for unofficial 'guides' in the souks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Then walk to the Kasbah Mosque area and explore the surrounding neighborhood. Head to the Mellah market for fresh produce and local life observation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or shared taxi (grand taxi) to the Majorelle Garden (~30 MAD bus fare). Entrance to Majorelle Garden is ~150 MAD — a beautiful cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjacent Berber Museum included in the ticket. Alternatively, visit the free Menara Gardens and olive grove for a budget-friendly nature break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina and explore the northern souks around Bab el-Khemis flea market area (open until late). Enjoy a relaxed evening at a rooftop café watching the Medina come alive at night.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast or street-side café — khobz bread, olive oil, and mint tea for ~25 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack near Majorelle — street sandwich (kefta or egg) and fresh-squeezed orange juice for ~30-40 MAD
meals.dinner: Affordable restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna — brochettes, salads, and bread for ~70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance to avoid queues. If budget is very tight, skip Majorelle and opt for the free Menara Gardens instead. Today is also a good day to arrange your Sahara desert tour — book through your riad or a reputable local agency for a 2-night/3-day group tour (~800-1200 MAD per person).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00-7:00 AM) via a shared group minibus for the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The journey takes approximately 8-9 hours through the stunning Atlas Mountains. Pass through the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) — breathtaking views. Stop at Aït Benhaddou UNESCO-listed ksar (ancient fortified village) for a 1-1.5 hour exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') — brief stop to see Taourirt Kasbah from the outside. Drive through the dramatic Draa Valley with its palm oases and kasbahs. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erfoud area by late afternoon. Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45-60 minute camel trek into the Erg Chebbi sand dunes. Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a dune — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Spend the night at a desert camp under the stars with a Berber bonfire, traditional music, and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at riad before departure — bread, jam, and tea for ~25 MAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside café in the Atlas Mountains — tagine for ~50-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Included at desert camp — traditional Berber meal of tagine, couscous, and mint tea (usually included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers — the Atlas Mountains can be cold in March and the desert is warm by day but cold at night (can drop to 5-10°C). Bring a scarf/shemagh for the camel ride. The shared group minibus tour typically costs 800-1,200 MAD per person for a 2-night desert package including transport, camp, and camel ride. Book 1-2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to hike the dunes and watch the spectacular Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence of the desert. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the edge of the dunes on foot and visit the small oasis village of Merzouga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities in Merzouga area (extra cost): quad biking on the dunes (~150-200 MAD/hour), sandboarding (~50 MAD rental), or visiting a nomadic Berber family. Alternatively, visit the Dayet Srji salt lake (free) near Merzouga where pink flamingos sometimes gather in spring. Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Todra Gorge or Dades Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the stunning Todra Gorge — dramatic 300-meter-high canyon walls. Short walk through the gorge (free). Continue driving toward Marrakech or overnight in a budget guesthouse in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate if the journey is split into two days.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Berber bread, olive oil, honey, argan jam, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Merzouga or Erfoud — tajine and bread for ~50-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Budget guesthouse dinner in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate — Moroccan meal for ~70-80 MAD (or included in extended tour package)

day_by_day.notes: March is an excellent time for the Sahara — warm days (25-30°C) and cool nights. Sunrise over Erg Chebbi is unmissable — set multiple alarms. If doing a 2-night desert package, tonight is the second night either at another camp or a guesthouse en route. Confirm return logistics with your tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey to Marrakech (approximately 4-5 hours from Ouarzazate, or 8-9 hours from Merzouga). If stopping in Ouarzazate, visit the Atlas Film Studios (entrance ~50 MAD) — the largest film studio in the world, used for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the Taourirt Kasbah (entrance ~20 MAD) — an impressive earthen fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Rest and freshen up at the riad. Visit the Marrakech Museum (Dar Menebhi Palace, entrance ~50 MAD) in the heart of the Medina — beautiful architecture and rotating art exhibitions. Explore the area around Place Ben Youssef.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a final evening in the Medina. Visit the Terrasse des Épices or a similar rooftop bar for sunset views. Explore the night souks and pick up last-minute souvenirs — argan oil, spices, leather goods, or Berber jewelry (bargain hard, start at 30-40% of asking price).

meals.breakfast: At guesthouse or roadside café en route — bread and mint tea for ~20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Quick roadside stop — sandwich or soup for ~30-40 MAD
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — a proper restaurant in the Medina for a full Moroccan feast (pastilla starter, lamb tagine, mint tea) for ~100-120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: If you bought souvenirs in the desert, keep receipts and pack carefully. Today is a good day to do any last-minute shopping in the souks. Confirm any remaining plans for Day 7 and check flight details. Tip your riad staff if service was good (50-100 MAD total is appropriate).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — wake up early for one last medina walk before the crowds arrive. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) — a 16th-century palace with rooftop views over the Medina and storks nesting on the walls. Explore the Mellah market one more time for fresh produce or local snacks to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time — visit the Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam (free, a pleasant garden with Wi-Fi) for a relaxing final afternoon. Alternatively, enjoy a final mint tea and people-watching session at a café on Jemaa el-Fna. Pack, check out of the riad, and arrange airport transfer (petit taxi ~50-70 MAD, negotiate before getting in or use a ride-hailing app).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international flights. Enjoy a final Moroccan coffee at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast or a beloved local café — msemen, honey, argan oil, and mint tea for ~30 MAD
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Medina or a final bowl of harira soup with dates and chebakia pastry for ~25-30 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or eat before departing — budget ~80-100 MAD for a final sit-down meal if time allows

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most riads is 11:00 AM — ask about luggage storage if your flight is later. Keep some MAD for the taxi and airport snacks. Morocco does not allow export of argan oil in large quantities without receipts — keep your purchase receipts. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately 2,500-3,500 MAD (~$250-350 USD) per person, including the desert tour.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Marrakech Boutique Stay in the Medina area (~20–30 min by taxi or pre-arranged transfer). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introduction to the Medina: stroll through the southern souks near Jemaa el-Fna square. Browse spice stalls, leather goods, and lantern shops without pressure to buy. Visit the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior) — the minaret is a perfect landmark to orient yourself. Keep the pace relaxed after your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jemaa el-Fna square at sunset to witness the famous transformation: food stalls, snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians fill the plaza. Grab a rooftop table at Café de France or Café Argana for mint tea with panoramic views over the square.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / airport snack
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near the hotel upon arrival — try a harira soup and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) at a local café for ~40–60 MAD
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — try grilled kefta, merguez sausages, and freshly squeezed orange juice. Budget ~80–120 MAD per person for a full spread

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotels for exchange rates). Save your energy — Day 2 is packed. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Medina streets are uneven cobblestone.

day_by_day.morning: Full Medina history deep-dive: Start at the Bahia Palace (9:00 AM, ~70 MAD entry) — a stunning 19th-century vizier's palace with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then walk to the nearby Badi Palace ruins (30 MAD entry) for sweeping views over the crumbling historic complex. End at the Saadian Tombs (70 MAD entry), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ben Youssef Madrasa (70 MAD entry), one of the finest examples of Islamic architecture in Morocco — the courtyard's zellige tilework and carved stucco are breathtaking. Wander the northern souks afterward: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' quarter), and the Souk Cherratin (leatherworkers). Bargaining is expected — start at 40–50% of the asking price.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant in the Medina. Try Le Foundouk or a similarly mid-range riad restaurant for a set menu featuring bastilla (pigeon or chicken pastry), lamb tagine, and pastilla au lait dessert. Book ahead if possible.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel or a nearby café — traditional Moroccan spread: msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, olives, and café au lait (~50–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a local restaurant near the souks — chicken tagine with olives and preserved lemon, served with khobz bread (~60–90 MAD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range riad restaurant dinner — set menu ~200–280 MAD per person including mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Bahia Palace early (before 10 AM) to beat tour groups. The Saadian Tombs can have queues — go right after Badi Palace. Carry a small daypack and stay hydrated; March afternoons can reach 22–26°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (garden entry ~150 MAD, museum ~100 MAD extra) — a vivid cobalt-blue botanical oasis designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) for the best light and fewer crowds. The adjacent Berber Museum within the garden is included in the entry fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for a culturally rich afternoon: explore the historic synagogues, the covered market, and the ornate balconied architecture. Visit the Museum of Moroccan Judaism if open. Then take a cooking class (mid-range options ~350–500 MAD per person) at one of the Medina's cooking schools — learn to make tagine, couscous, and Moroccan salads with a local chef.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening: hammam experience at a traditional local hammam (not a tourist spa) — try Hammam Mouassine or a similar authentic bathhouse (~50–100 MAD for the full scrub and soap treatment). Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner near your riad.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Majorelle Garden — avocado toast and fresh juice are now widely available in the Gueliz/Ville Nouvelle area (~70–100 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the cooking class, or eat your own creations! Alternatively, grab a sandwich marocain from a street stall near the Mellah (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a neighborhood restaurant near the Medina — try pastilla or a slow-cooked lamb shank tagine (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance online or through your hotel. The hammam is best enjoyed in the late afternoon/early evening. Women and men typically use separate sections or have separate time slots at traditional hammams.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:30–7:00 AM) by private driver or shared 4x4 transfer toward Merzouga and the Sahara Desert — a scenic 8–9 hour drive crossing the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at the Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) — a stunning red-mud citadel used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones (~10 MAD entry, 1.5 hrs).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and rose-growing villages (Kelaat M'Gouna). Stop briefly in Ouarzazate ('the door of the desert') for lunch and a quick peek at the Atlas Film Studios exterior. Continue driving through the Dades Valley and Todra Gorge area toward Merzouga, arriving at your desert camp/guesthouse by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute camel trek into the dunes (included in most camp packages or ~150–200 MAD separately). Watch the sun set over the Sahara from the top of a dune — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel in Marrakech before departure — pack snacks and water for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate — try a local restaurant near the kasbah for a lamb tagine or Berber omelette (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp under the stars — usually a set menu of harira, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan sweets (typically included in camp fee or ~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book a private driver or shared transfer in advance — this is a long driving day (~450 km). A private driver costs ~800–1,200 MAD and offers more flexibility. Bring layers: the desert can be surprisingly cold at night in March (5–10°C). Sunscreen and a hat are essential for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to hike or ride to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes and watch the sun rise over the Sahara — an absolutely unmissable, otherworldly experience. Photograph the rippling sand patterns in the golden morning light. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast of mint tea, msemen, and honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Merzouga area: visit the village of Khamlia to hear Gnawa music performed by the local community (a small tip/donation is appreciated). Option to rent a quad bike or go sandboarding on the dunes (~150–250 MAD). Visit a local nomad family's tent for an authentic cultural exchange and tea ceremony, arranged through your camp.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech via a different scenic route through the Ziz Valley and Midelt, or spend a second night in the desert (recommended if budget allows). If returning, depart by 2:00 PM to arrive in Marrakech by 11:00 PM. If staying a second night, enjoy another magical evening around a campfire with Berber drumming and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp — mint tea, msemen, honey, argan oil, and soft-boiled eggs (included in camp stay)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Merzouga village — try a Berber pizza (medfouna, a stuffed bread) or tagine (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner (if staying second night) or roadside restaurant dinner on the return journey to Marrakech (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune experience is the highlight of the entire trip — set multiple alarms. Sandboarding boards can be rented from camp staff. If returning to Marrakech same day, this is a very long day; consider an overnight stop in Ouarzazate to break the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Marrakech (if not already back) or enjoy a recovery morning in the city. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (70 MAD entry) housed in a 19th-century palace — excellent collection of Moroccan art, coins, and manuscripts. Wander the quieter northern Medina alleyways around Mouassine neighborhood — beautiful fountains, artisan workshops, and hidden riads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip or half-day excursion to the Ourika Valley (~30 km from Marrakech) — a lush Berber valley in the High Atlas foothills with a cascading waterfall, local Berber villages, and a weekly market (Mondays are market day, but the valley is beautiful any day). Hire a grand taxi for the round trip (~150–200 MAD shared, or ~300–400 MAD private). Walk to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (7 short cascades, ~30 min hike up).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — splurge slightly on dinner at a beautiful riad restaurant for a memorable last night. Try Dar Yacout, Nomad, or a similar atmospheric spot. After dinner, one last stroll through Jemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere and pick up any last souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a patisserie in the Medina — try a café near the Mouassine fountain for coffee and almond croissants (~50–70 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Ourika Valley — fresh trout from the mountain streams is a local specialty at valley restaurants (~100–150 MAD including drinks)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-to-upper-range riad restaurant — budget ~250–350 MAD per person for a full Moroccan feast with wine or cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley is very popular on weekends — go early to avoid crowds. Wear sturdy shoes for the waterfall hike as the path can be slippery. Bargain hard for taxis and agree on the price before getting in. The Medina is busiest on Saturday evenings — embrace the energy!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the El Badi Palace one more time at sunrise if you haven't, or explore the Mellah's Sunday market. Browse the Rahba Kedima (spice square) for last-minute gifts: saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, and rose water are excellent souvenirs. Head to the tanneries near Bab Debbagh for a final look at this ancient leather-dyeing craft (free to view from rooftop shops, which will try to sell you leather goods).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight: if afternoon/evening flight — pack up, check out, and transfer to the airport with time to spare (allow 2 hours before departure). If late flight — store luggage at the hotel and enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Browse the fixed-price Ensemble Artisanal cooperative near the Koutoubia for fairly priced crafts with no bargaining required.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week spanning imperial history, Saharan dunes, Berber culture, mountain valleys, and the sensory overload of the world's most vibrant medina.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy every last drop of mint tea and bite of msemen
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the souks or a sandwich from a bakery for ~30–50 MAD — save room for airport snacks
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or an early dinner in the Medina before heading to the airport — try a simple harira and pastilla one last time (~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 90 minutes to get to the airport and through security — Marrakech airport can be busy. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. Keep a small amount of MAD for tips and last-minute purchases. Most importantly: start planning your return trip — Morocco has a way of pulling you back.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Marrakech Boutique Stay in a chauffeured vehicle with welcome refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into the boutique riad. Enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a brief orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the immediate neighbourhood of the Medina to acclimatize — explore the vibrant lanes near Mouassine Quarter, browsing artisan workshops and spice stalls at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop aperitif at the riad as the sun sets over the Medina skyline and Atlas Mountains. Private guided evening walk through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square to witness the legendary storytellers, musicians, and food stalls come alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the riad upon check-in — Moroccan mezze, fresh juices, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk — a celebrated heritage restaurant set in a restored caravanserai near the souks, offering refined Moroccan cuisine including bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine, and house-made pastilla dessert

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep pace gentle to recover from travel. Confirm next-day excursion logistics with concierge. March weather in Marrakech is mild and pleasant (18–24°C), ideal for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Bahia Palace and El Badi Palace ruins — explore the opulent 19th-century architecture, ornate zellige tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and vast sunken gardens with an expert historian guide. Skip-the-line access included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive visit to the Saadian Tombs followed by a curated walk through the ancient Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its covered spice souks. Transition to a private hands-on cooking class at a premium culinary atelier in the Medina — learn to prepare harira soup, lamb mrouzia, and orange-blossom bastilla under a master chef.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive hammam and spa ritual at a luxury heritage hammam — traditional black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the riad for a private candlelit dinner on the rooftop terrace.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Moroccan breakfast at the riad — msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, fresh-pressed orange juice, and Berber omelette
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices overlooking the Rahba Kedima spice square — seasonal salads, kefta brochettes, and fresh lemonade with rose water
meals.dinner: Private rooftop dinner at the riad prepared by an in-house chef — three-course tasting menu with Moroccan wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina exploration. The cooking class typically runs 2–3 hours and includes a printed recipe booklet to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Private day excursion departs early by luxury 4x4 toward the Atlas Mountains. Stop at the Kik Plateau for panoramic views over the Haouz Plain. Visit the Berber village of Imlil nestled at the foot of Mount Toubkal — meet a local family for a traditional Berber tea welcome and explore the terraced walnut and apple orchards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike through Aït Mizane valley with a certified mountain guide — moderate trail passing through traditional villages and ancient irrigation channels (seguias). Option to ride mules for a more leisurely experience. Picnic lunch prepared with local ingredients served in a scenic valley setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by late afternoon. Sunset cocktails at La Mamounia's iconic Churchill Bar or Garden Terrace — one of Morocco's most legendary luxury hotels, open to non-staying guests for drinks. Dinner at a top-tier Marrakech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the riad before departure — croissants, Moroccan pastries, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet mountain picnic in the Imlil valley — prepared hamper with kefta wraps, roasted vegetable salads, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and Moroccan pastries
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout — a legendary palatial restaurant in the Medina with live Andalusian music, multiple dining salons, and an extensive menu of classic Moroccan royal cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Bring layers for the Atlas Mountains — temperatures can be 5–8°C cooler than Marrakech at altitude. Sturdy walking shoes essential. Depart by 08:00 to maximise time in the mountains.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech by private luxury vehicle on the legendary road to the Sahara — the scenic N9 route over the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m), the highest paved mountain pass in North Africa. Stop at panoramic viewpoints and a traditional Berber roadside cooperative selling handwoven carpets and argan products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the cinematic Draa Valley and the ancient fortified ksar of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and iconic film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia). Private guided tour of the earthen citadel with a local expert historian. Cross the river by foot to explore the inhabited village.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga or Zagora (depending on route preference). Check in to a luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge. Welcome sunset camel trek into the dunes of Erg Chebbi — ride to a prime dune crest to watch the sun melt into the sand sea.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the riad before checkout and departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, fresh Moroccan salads, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — communal fire, live Gnawa and Berber drumming, lantern-lit dining tent with harira, mechoui (whole roasted lamb), and dessert pastries

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~6–7 hours driving with stops). Depart Marrakech by 08:00. The road over Tizi n'Tichka is spectacular but winding — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive. Confirm desert camp reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private sunrise camel or 4x4 excursion to the highest dune crest — watch the Sahara ignite in gold and amber as the sun rises over the Algerian border. Return to camp for a peaceful breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided walk with a Tuareg nomad to learn desert navigation and survival traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and travel toward the Todra Gorge — a dramatic canyon with 300-metre limestone walls carved by the Todra River. Private guided walk through the narrowest sections of the gorge. Visit a local Berber cooperative for a rug-weaving demonstration and the opportunity to commission bespoke pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in the Dadès Valley or Skoura oasis. Sunset walk through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs — ancient earthen fortresses glowing terracotta in the fading light. Private rooftop dinner at the kasbah with views over the palm oasis.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — Berber bread baked in embers, honey, argan oil, fresh fruit, and coffee over the open fire
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant at the mouth of Todra Gorge — grilled trout from the local river, Moroccan salads, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Private dinner at the luxury kasbah — chef's tasting menu featuring regional specialties including pastilla with wild mushrooms, lamb with preserved lemon, and rose-water crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: March mornings in the Sahara can be cool (8–12°C before sunrise) — bring a warm layer for the sunrise excursion. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in morning or late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the kasbah — optional yoga session on the rooftop terrace or a private spa treatment using local argan and rose products. Explore the Skoura palm oasis on horseback or by bicycle — a lush labyrinth of date palms, pomegranate trees, and ancient irrigation channels tended by Berber farmers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) — famous for its vast damask rose fields, most fragrant in spring. Visit a traditional rose water distillery to see the artisanal extraction process and purchase premium rose products. Continue through the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka or alternate Tizi n'Test pass.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Freshen up at the riad. Exclusive private dinner at a premier Marrakech restaurant for a celebratory penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the kasbah — fresh-baked msemen, local honey, goat cheese, Medjool dates, and Atlas mountain herbal tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Roses Valley prepared by the kasbah — artisan bread, cured meats, local olives, cheese, and seasonal fruit amid the rose fields
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nomad Marrakech (rooftop) or Al Fassia Aguedal — renowned for authentic Fassi cuisine prepared by an all-female team; highlights include pigeon pastilla, seven-vegetable couscous, and honey-glazed lamb

day_by_day.notes: March is the very beginning of rose season in the Roses Valley — early blooms may be visible. The full bloom peaks in late April/May. Confirm road conditions for the return pass with your driver.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — private guided tour of the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent YSL Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). The electric-blue garden, designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, is a world-class landmark. The museum showcases the designer's deep love affair with Morocco through fashion, art, and archives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Curated luxury shopping experience in the Medina souks with a personal shopping guide — navigate the labyrinthine lanes to source the finest handmade leather goods at Chouara Tannery artisans, bespoke Berber jewellery, hand-knotted carpets, and artisan ceramics. Visit a prestigious carpet house for a private viewing and tasting of mint tea. Final packing and checkout from the riad.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails on the riad rooftop or at a chic Guéliz neighbourhood bar. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure flight — private chauffeured transfer with luggage assistance.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate farewell breakfast at the riad — full spread of Moroccan pastries, fresh juices, eggs to order, amlou, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pepe Nero — a sophisticated fusion restaurant blending Italian and Moroccan flavours in an elegant Medina setting; ideal for a refined final lunch
meals.dinner: Depending on departure time: farewell dinner at Dar Zellij, a 17th-century palace restaurant with live Andalusian music, or a gourmet airport lounge experience if flight departs early evening

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can be busy — book timed entry tickets in advance through the concierge. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours at the airport before international departure. Ensure all artisan purchases are properly wrapped and receipts obtained for customs. A truly immersive 7-day journey blending imperial history, Berber culture, and Saharan adventure at the highest level of comfort.
